Visa in Talks to Acquire Fireblocks for ~$2.5 Billion to Expand Crypto Presence According to Axios, Visa is in talks to acquire crypto custody infrastructure firm Fireblocks in a deal that would value the company at around $2.5 billion. If finalized, the transaction would further expand Visa's footprint in digital asset custody and blockchain-based payment infrastructure. The reports remain subject to further confirmation, and the specific terms and progress of the acquisition negotiations have not been disclosed. In a statement to The Block, Fireblocks stated, "This is news to us, and not true at present time." Meanwhile, Visa stated that the company does not comment on rumors or speculation. — link

Circle Shareholder Sues Trump and World Liberty Over UAE-Linked Deals, Alleging Unconstitutional Profits According to Bloomberg, a Circle shareholder has sued President Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial, alleging that Trump violated the U.S. Constitution’s Foreign Emoluments Clause through two UAE-linked transactions: the $500 million sale of a 49% stake in World Liberty and a $2 billion Binance investment funded using its USD1 stablecoin. The plaintiff claims the deals harmed Circle investors through unfair competition and seeks the return of alleged illegal profits and damages. Circle said it was not involved in the lawsuit, while World Liberty denied the allegations. — link

Polymarket Fires CMO Matthew Modabber Amid Fake Promotion Claims and CFTC Probe Polymarket has fired Matthew Modabber, its chief marketing officer since January 2024 and a close associate of CEO Shayne Coplan, the New York Post reported, citing sources. The company launched an internal investigation over allegations that his team produced fake trading-profit promotional content and paid influencers through personal accounts. The incidents have triggered a CFTC investigation, which remains ongoing. No wrongdoing has been established. Polymarket declined to comment. Modabber did not respond to a request for comment. — link
